mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT suppresses discretionary shopping trips, so retail and recreation stays below the prior four-week average over the next month. The mechanism works through reduced weekday foot traffic and fails if retail rebounds despite no recovery in commuting mobility.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain near their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent near home, which diverts trips away from retail and recreation venues and lowers RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks. The effect reverses if higher residential time coincides with stronger shopping activity instead of substitution.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 3% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL stays above 3% for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility jumps while TRANSIT stays weak, households are reallocating outing time toward outdoor leisure rather than retail spending, which pushes RETAIL_REC down over the next month. The signal fails if park visits rise together with stronger transit use and retail does not weaken.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days when PARKS stays elevated and TRANSIT stays below its recent average.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM is flat to slightly negative while RETAIL_REC is already weak, consumers are conserving nonessential spending and the retail-and-recreation series will remain lower over the next four weeks. This mechanism fails when grocery trips recover without any improvement in retail demand.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays below 0 for at least 2 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining below 0 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A widening gap between RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES implies stay-at-home behavior and fewer discretionary outings, which should depress RETAIL_REC within one week. The signal disappears if residential time rises without a concurrent workplace decline.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds WORKPLACES by at least 30 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not drop in the next 7 days when RESIDENTIAL is at least 30 points above WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in TRANSIT combined with stable or improving WORKPLACES mobility lifts access to shopping corridors and supports higher RETAIL_REC over the next month. The claim fails if commuting mobility improves but retail remains below its recent average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise from current levels.

mechanism_narrative: An elevated PARKS series relative to RETAIL_REC captures a weather- or season-driven shift toward outdoor leisure that crowds out indoor shopping trips, lowering RETAIL_REC after a two-week lag. The hypothesis fails if parks activity stays high but retail also strengthens.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 20 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after PARKS exceeds 20 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES remains depressed and TRANSIT does not recover, weekday circulation stays constrained and the retail sector keeps losing spontaneous visits, so RETAIL_REC should remain below the prior four-week mean over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if retail rebounds without any commuting recovery.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays below -25 and TRANSIT stays below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its last-28-day average over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES stays below -25 and TRANSIT stays below -20.
